notes: iFixit's launch-era PlayStation 4 teardown prints no model number; its power supply is the ADP-240AR, which iFixit lists for CUH-10XXA models (it lists a different supply, the ADP-240CR, for CUH-11XXA models), so later revisions can differ. TechInfoDepot's CUH-1001A page names the same SoC, GDDR5, serial flash and Wi-Fi chips.

gaps: The teardown prints no model number. The CUH-10xx tie rests on the power supply label (ADP-240AR, read in the full-size step 13 photo) and iFixit's listing for CUH-10XXA models, plus the chip match to TechInfoDepot's CUH-1001A page.
TechInfoDepot also gives CPU MPN CXD90044GB, GDDR5 K4G80325FB, a 1 TB drive and a Wi-Fi chip 88W8897M, which conflict with iFixit's teardown; iFixit's text is used throughout.
FCC ID AK8CUH100C1 appears on TechInfoDepot only; fccid.io and fcc.report returned HTTP 403 to the researcher, so it is not in the fcc field.
The optical drive model is not named in the guide, so none is claimed. The laser entry rests only on the laser caution label on the drive in the step 15 photo.
Left out: the hard drive (step 7: HGST 500 GB 2.5 in SATA, user-replaceable), because there is no hard drive part type.
The SoC is filed under ic_mcu, the nearest part type. '8-core' was dropped from its spec because only step 1 (expected specs) says it.
Retailer listings give other ADP-240AR outputs that conflict with the label; they are not used.
Chip names are as printed in iFixit's teardown; nothing was checked on a board.
Datasheets: Macronix MX25L25635F and ROHM BD7763EFV only. None found for the Samsung GDDR5 and DDR3 chips, the Marvell 88W8797, the CXD90026G or the Macronix 25L1006E.
Years: 2013 comes from TechInfoDepot's May 2013 manufacture date and 22 July 2013 FCC approval date; no end of production is given.
method: iFixit PlayStation 4 Teardown (guide 19493): PDF export (23 pages) read with tools/research.js pdf, plus the API text; the step 13 label photo was read at full size (3486 px wide).
iFixit ADP-240AR power supply listing (IF297-008-1): input 100-240VAC 2.5A 50-60Hz, 'compatible with the CUH-10XXA model', and a note that the ADP-240CR is for CUH-11XXA.
TechInfoDepot wiki page for the PS4 (CUH-1001A): model, FCC ID, manufacture and approval dates, chip names.
Macronix MX25L25635F datasheet (rev 1.5; its ordering table lists MX25L25635FMI-10G) and ROHM BD7763EFV datasheet: both open as PDFs.
LCSC and ROHM product pages open, but LCSC's datasheet PDF link returns an HTML page, so it is not cited.
Refused to the researcher: fccid.io and fcc.report (HTTP 403).

comps.spec: SCEI CXD90026G SoC with AMD 'Jaguar' CPU cores and an AMD Radeon GPU (step 19)
Samsung K4G41325FC-HC03 4 Gb (512 MB) GDDR5 RAM; steps 19 and 20 each list 8 chips (8 x 512 MB = 4 GB), 16 in all
Macronix MX25L25635FMI 256 Mb serial flash (step 19) and Macronix 25L1006E CMOS serial flash (step 20)
Marvell Avastar 88W8797 integrated 2x2 WLAN, Bluetooth and FM single-chip SoC (step 21)
ROHM BD7763EFV motor driver IC on the Blu-ray drive board (step 16)
Laser in the slot-loading Blu-ray/DVD drive (step 3): the drive carries a laser caution label, class 2 laser radiation when open (step 15 photo)
Heat sink stuck to the EMI shielding over the board; iFixit could not separate the two (step 22)

Internal power supply, Sony ADP-240AR, read from the label in the step 13 photo: AC input 100-240 V~ 2.5 A 50/60 Hz; DC output 12 V and 4.7 V mode is +12 V 17 A with +4.7 V 3 A, 12 V only mode is +12 V 18.6 A with +4.7 V 0 A
